Dar opinião, passo a passo: Giving your opinion, step by step
PASSO 1: para dar opinião, use um verbo: STEP 1: to give your opinion, use a verb of opinion + «dass»: «Ich finde, dass Homeoffice praktisch ist» (I think working from home is practical). STEP 2: with NORMAL word order (no «dass»), the opinion sounds more direct — just like English "I think working from home is practical": «Ich finde, Homeoffice ist praktisch.» STEP 3: «MEINER MEINUNG NACH» (in my opinion) opens the sentence, and the verb comes right after (2nd position): «Meiner Meinung nach ist das richtig.» STEP 4: «Ich bin der Meinung, dass …» is formal; «Ich finde / glaube / denke / meine» is everyday. Careful: «ich meine» means "I think / I mean (my opinion)", not just "I mean" as a filler. STEP 5: ALWAYS back it up with «weil», «denn», «deshalb» or an example: «Ich finde das gut, weil man Zeit spart.» STEP 6: soften when needed: «Ich glaube eher, dass …» (I rather think that…), «Es kommt darauf an» (it depends).

Concordar e discordar com educação, pass: Agreeing and disagreeing politely, step by step
PASSO 1: para CONCORDAR: «Da stimme ich: STEP 1: to AGREE: «Da stimme ich dir zu» (I agree with you), «Das sehe ich genauso» (I see it the same way), «Da hast du recht» (you're right — German "has" right), «Das stimmt» (that's true). STEP 2: to agree PARTLY: «Da stimme ich dir teilweise zu», «Einerseits hast du recht, andererseits …». STEP 3: to DISAGREE politely: «Das sehe ich anders» (I see it differently), «Da bin ich nicht sicher», «Das stimmt nicht ganz» (that's not quite right). STEP 4: to DISAGREE strongly: «Da bin ich anderer Meinung», «Das sehe ich überhaupt nicht so». STEP 5: «zustimmen» takes the DATIVE and is separable: «Ich stimme dir zu», «Ich habe ihm zugestimmt». STEP 6: «dafür sein» (be in favor) and «dagegen sein» (be against), with «dass» or «zu»: «Ich bin dafür, dass wir früher anfangen.»
Separable: the prefix goes to the end.

O texto de opinião, passo a passo: The opinion text, step by step
PASSO 1: um texto de opinião (fórum, car: STEP 1: an opinion text (a forum post, a letter to the editor) has FOUR parts: INTRODUCTION (the topic and your position), ARGUMENTS (two or three, with reasons), an EXAMPLE (a concrete case) and a CONCLUSION. STEP 2: introduction: «Ich möchte meine Meinung zum Thema … äußern» (I'd like to share my opinion on…). STEP 3: arguments, in order: «ERSTENS …, ZWEITENS …, DRITTENS …» (first, second, third), «AUSSERDEM …» (besides). STEP 4: example: «Zum Beispiel …», «Ein Beispiel dafür ist …». STEP 5: counterargument: «Natürlich gibt es auch Nachteile, aber …» (of course there are downsides too, but…). STEP 6: conclusion: «Zusammenfassend kann man sagen, dass …» (to sum up…), «Abschließend möchte ich sagen …» (in conclusion…). STEP 7: use the connectors you've learned (weil, denn, deshalb, obwohl, trotzdem, einerseits … andererseits) — and remember each one's word order.

Two colleagues debate working from home.

— Concordo em parte. Economiza-se tempo,: — I partly agree. You save time, because you don't have to commute.
— Além disso, pode-se trabalhar com mais: — Besides, you can work more calmly.
— Vejo diferente. Em casa muita coisa me: — I see it differently. At home, lots of things distract me.
— Por exemplo, a roupa, a TV e os vizinh: — For example, the laundry, the TV and the neighbors.
— Por um lado você tem razão, por outro: — On the one hand you're right; on the other, you can organize yourself well.
— Resumindo, eu diria: uma mistura dos d: — To sum up, I'd say a mix of both is ideal.
